subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards stay full-content-only with a stronger coalescing or transport fix, or should OpenClaw add an explicit opt-in append/delta mode for deployments where full-content CardKit updates are too slow?
rationale: Current main preserves cumulative CardKit payloads to prevent truncation, but reporter evidence says full-content payload growth still creates severe latency and a live comment says the linked coalescing-only PR did not materially improve it.

options.title: Require A Revised Feishu Strategy
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a revised fix with live Feishu or production-boundary timing proof before accepting either coalescing or append-mode behavior.

options.title: Accept Coalescing Direction
options.body: Continue with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91943 as the canonical path, but require conflict resolution and exact-head proof that it fixes the live latency tail.

options.title: Approve Opt-In Append Mode
options.body: Allow a documented plugin-owned append/delta option that keeps full-content as the default and proves the truncation risk is isolated to opt-in deployments.

recommendation.title: Require A Revised Feishu Strategy
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a revised fix with live Feishu or production-boundary timing proof before accepting either coalescing or append-mode behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu package metadata names this handle as the community-maintained package contact, and this is a Feishu plugin behavior decision.
